comments.content: The new `_log_transaction_async` implementation acquires `self._lock` and then awaits `asyncio.gather(*tasks)`. This can cause a deadlock if any of the awaited `log_transaction` tasks need to acquire the same lock (directly or indirectly). More importantly, `_get_result` already holds `self._lock` when it calls `await self._log_transaction_async(...)`, so this method will try to re-acquire a non-reentrant `asyncio.Lock` and deadlock. The lock acquisition should be removed from `_log_transaction_async`, or the callers should not hold the lock when invoking it.

`asyncio.gather(*tasks)` without `return_exceptions=True` will propagate the first exception raised by any completed logging task. Since these are background logging tasks, a logging failure should not break the main result retrieval path. Consider using `return_exceptions=True` or wrapping the gather in a try/except to prevent logging errors from propagating.

The `except asyncio.CancelledError` block cancels pending tasks and re-raises, but the tasks were already removed from `self.log_transaction_tasks` by `self.log_transaction_tasks.clear()` before the gather. The subsequent loop over `self.log_transaction_tasks` in the outer `except asyncio.CancelledError` (lines 654-659) will therefore not see those tasks. This is inconsistent with the intent of cleaning up pending tasks on cancellation.
